- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price drop is steep.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 70+), model tends to lag; add 1–2% downward bias for next 7–14 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter: average last 5 days’ sentiment to adjust forecast weight.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model may misread trend; favor 3–5 day moving average of price + sentiment for correction.
